records.our_prose: In the Piedmont and Coastal Plain, sow sweet corn straight into the garden after your last frost, once the soil feels warm. You can keep sowing every couple of weeks into midsummer for a longer harvest instead of one big batch. Always plant corn in a block of several short rows rather than one long row; the wind carries pollen from plant to plant, and a block pollinates far better than a line.

A block of short rows pollinates far better than a single long row.

records.our_prose: In St. George, direct-sow sweet corn once, at the front of the spring window from about March 15 to April 5 per USU Extension, once the last frost has passed. Ears are ready to pick from late May, over about a five-week window as the different sowing dates catch up; corn does best planted in blocks of at least four short rows so the wind pollinates every ear. There is no fall corn crop here; this is a single spring planting.

records.source_context: If the soil becomes too dry, their growth may be seriously limited. Most vegetable crops require 1 inch of water per week for optimum pro- duction. If your area does not receive this amount of rainfall each week during the growing season, you will need to irrigate your garden using overhead sprinklers, soaker hoses, drip tape or hand watering.
